page: Amazon Web Services m6i.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (Ice Lake 8375C). Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core, running at a clock frequency of 3.5 GHz. It includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 54 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI) alongside cryptographic acceleration features such as AES-NI and SHA extensions.

System memory comprises 64 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached Elastic Block Store volumes for non-volatile operations. Baseline network throughput is rated at 6 Gbps, and no discrete graphics hardware is present on this platform.

Benchmark measurements position the m6i.4xlarge consistently within the median range across compute, memory, and application-level workloads. It achieves a multi-core Geekbench score of 9,695 alongside 15,070 in multi-core stress-ng tests. Large-block memory reads operate at 97.93 GB/sec and writes at 57.44 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 15.63 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 21.5 GB/sec static web serving throughput. For CPU-based machine learning inference, it processes 1,103 prompt tokens per second on lightweight 135M parameter models and 32.6 tokens per second on 7B models.

The 1:4 core-to-memory configuration delivers standard resource density for containerized application clusters, mid-sized relational and in-memory databases, continuous integration builders, and general enterprise backend applications. The absence of local solid-state storage requires architectural consideration of remote storage bandwidth limits, but the dedicated compute threads and AVX-512 support provide consistent processing reliability.
description: Amazon Web Services m6i.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs spanning 8 physical cores at 3.5 GHz, paired with 64 GB of DDR4 memory at 3 GHz, establishing a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Hardware support includes AVX-512 with VNNI for accelerated vector computing. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, depending entirely on network block storage, and operates without discrete GPUs. Network throughput provides a 6 Gbps baseline. Benchmark outcomes place the server in the middle tiers for raw compute, memory bandwidth, and caching operations, demonstrated by 15.63 million Redis SET operations per second and 9,695 Geekbench multi-core points. This profile is engineered for general backend services, medium-tier web platforms, containerized environments, and enterprise database hosting.
